summary: The school district urges the FCC to preserve and strengthen the E-Rate program, emphasizing the program's essential role in supporting modern public education and the potential cost implications of reducing or eliminating it. The parent guardian urges the FCC to protect E-Rate funding and ensure public schools can provide students with reliable, affordable connectivity, rejecting proposals to sunset or eliminate the program and narrowing eligibility criteria.

claims.requested_action: Reject proposals to sunset or eliminate E-Rate program
claims.argument: Rejecting sunset proposals would preserve the program's funding and continuity
claims.evidence_quote: I therefore respectfully urge the Commission to: Reject any proposal to sunset or eliminate the E-Rate program; Reject proposals that would unnecessarily narrow E-Rate eligibility or restrict support based solely on geography or other criteria that would leave students without adequate support; Preserve support for the connectivity and internal network infrastructure schools need to provide reliable educational access; and Work with schools and other stakeholders to strengthen and modernize E-Rate rather than reduce its role in public education. E-Rate has enabled schools (public and private) and libraries to build and maintain the connectivity necessary for students and patrons to participate fully in modern education. As our nation seeks to prepare students for college, careers, and an increasingly technology-driven economy, now is not the time to undermine the very program and related infrastructure that makes those opportunities possible. Our students deserve access to the tools they need to learn and succeed regardless of where they live or their family’s financial circumstances. I urge the Commission to protect E-Rate and ensure that public schools can continue providing students with reliable, affordable, and effective connectivity. Thank you for considering my comments. Yours in Education, Dr. Tony Shinall Superintendent Princeville Community Unit School District #326
